blocks.text: View from above of a historic church and tiled rooftops around a square in Cusco, Peru
Cusco, Peru: a historic church and tiled rooftops around the square, seen from above

Breakfast. Your guide will confirm the meeting time. An English-speaking escort will meet you in the lobby and take you to the railway station. The Expedition train takes you to Aguas Calientes, the village at the foot of Machu Picchu that is also known as Machu Picchu Pueblo.

At Machu Picchu, you’ll walk among stone terraces, temples and ceremonial plazas. The name means ‘Old Mountain’ in Quechua. The city was built on a ridge in the Andes in the 15th century. Its remote location helped preserve the buildings during the Spanish conquest, when many other Inca settlements were destroyed.

Hiram Bingham’s expedition in 1911 brought Machu Picchu to wider attention outside Peru, although local residents had long known about it. During the tour, your guide will explain the city’s history, architecture and engineering. Machu Picchu has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1983 and was named one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007.

Lunch at a restaurant. Then return to the station for the train to Cusco. Transfer to Xima Cusco 4★ or a comparable hotel. Overnight in Cusco.
